name: Oakham Castle Great Hall

dates.altered: Two red oak beams put into part of the roof by 'George Villies, Duke of Buckingham'; three later dormers; modern additions built on to the west. Used as the Assize Court and then as the Magistrates Court.
dates.note: The entry's 'probably built by Walkelin de Ferrers circa 1180-90' agrees with the node's exemplar year of 1185 to within its own hedge.

refs.title: Oakham Castle
refs.note: Grade I. The Details section opens with the legacy header 'SK 8608 6/2 8.5.50. 1469 MARKET PLACE Oakham Castle I'. A search result printed 'List Entry Number: 1073277. Date first listed: 08-May-1950.' The entry closes 'Scheduled AM.'

survey.prepared: The Details section's own legacy header: 'SK 8608 6/2 8.5.50. 1469 MARKET PLACE Oakham Castle I'.

quotes.text: Rectangular ward enclosed by high bank containing fine arcaded Hall in transitional style, probably built by Walkelin de Ferrers circa 1180-90. Stone used is fine-grained shelly oolite from Clipsham. Stone slate roof, 3 later dormers 65 ft by 44 ft.
quotes.page: Official list entry, Details, opening paragraph

quotes.text: The hall is divided by 3 shafts on either side into 4 bays, 8 paired windows under pointed arch, stone band continues cills. Round-headed doorway now in centre formerly at East End. At East gable end 3 blocked doorways, simple continuous moulding.
quotes.page: Official list entry, Details, hall description

quotes.text: Circular piers and crocketed capitals like those in the chancel at Canterbury. Carved figures of musicians in spandrels. Romanesque carved wall corbels.
quotes.page: Official list entry, Details, hall description

quotes.text: part of roof 2 red oak beams put in by George Villies, Duke of Buckingham.

measurements.name: overall_width_ft
measurements.note: THE SUBJECT OF THIS DIMENSION IS NOT STATED. The legacy text runs the roof, the dormers and the figures into one sentence -- 'Stone slate roof, 3 later dormers 65 ft by 44 ft' -- with no verb attaching the pair to anything. The only structure the entry describes is the arcaded hall, so the figures are almost certainly its plan; that is a reading and is marked as one. The first figure printed is taken as the width, per the corpus convention where a front is unstated.
